Brain MRI was normal, but the spinal cord MRI displayed a continuous long segment of T2WI hyperintensity in the ventral horns of grey matter in the upper and mid-thoracic cord with no intervening normal cord (Figures 2 and 3). Remainder of the grey matter in the involved segments and the spinal cord white matter were normal. There was no evidence of post-contrast enhancement (Figure 4). The imaging features were suggestive of viral myelitis.

in_text_mentions: IgG (Table 1), and the serum contained WNV IgG at 4.3 mg/dL and a WNV IgM of 6.33 mg/dL, both of which are positive (Table 2). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain was normal. A spine MRI showed a linear hyperintensity lesion beginning at the level of T7 and extending to the conus medullaris, restricted to the central gray matter of the spinal cord (Figure 1). Strikingly, an axial MRI displayed selective involvement of the ventral gray matter, sparing the long tracts (Figure 2). On follow-up after several weeks, the patient continues to experience debilitating weakness and backaches.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: The panel shows axial T2-weighted imaging of the cervical spine demonstrating T2 hyperintensity confined to the anterior horn cells, which is a characteristic finding for acute flaccid myelitis. B: The panel shows axial T1 postcontrast imaging of the cervical spine with evidence of nerve root enhancement, a recognized finding in the progression of acute flaccid myelitis. C: The panel demonstrates sagittal T2-weighted imaging of the cervical spine showing extensive longitudinal T2 hyperintensity involving the central cord, highly characteristic of acute flaccid myelitis. D: The panel shows sagittal T1 postcontrast imaging of the dorsolumbar spine demonstrating enhancement of the ventral cauda equina nerve roots, consistent with active inflammatory processes in acute flaccid myelitis.

panels.figure_caption: Spinal magnetic resonance imaging performed four days after the onset of symptoms. T2-weighted (A and C) and T1 postcontrast images (B and D) showing central cord T2 hyperintensity involving almost the whole central cervical cord (arrowheads in C). Axial images demonstrate T2 hyperintensity confined to the anterior horn cells asymmetric to the right (white arrows in A) and nerve root enhancement (white arrows in B). Normal aspect of the dorsolumbar cord till the conus medullaris with ventral cauda equina nerve roots enhancement (arrowheads in D).
